newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures close lackluster day higher.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures close lackluster day higher.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended a lackluster session higher after U.S. long bond yields slipped below the key psychological seven percent level, traders and analysts said.
However, they expect the rally in currency futures to be short-lived.
"The dollar is gathering its breath for another upturn," one currency futures source said.
He said dollar buying was heavy in the last several days, and funds and dealers who are short want to buy dollars at lower prices.
He expects such buying to emerge once June marks rise to $0.5833 to $0.5837, which currently corresponds to 1.7190 to 1.7200 spot.
Likewise, dollar buyers will emerge once June yen rises to $0.007960, which is equivalent to 126.50 spot.

Several traders said a smaller than expected rise in the U.S. first-quarter employment cost index, coupled with a drop in U.S. March durable goods orders, could provide the dollar with more downside momentum in overnight trade.
The employment cost index rose 0.6 percent, below average trade expectations for a 0.9 percent rise and against a 1996 fourth-quarter gain of 0.8 percent.

U.S. durable goods orders fell 3.0 percent, their largest decline since August 1996, compared with average trade estimates of unchanged. Goods excluding defense dropped 2.6 percent from February, compared with traders' estimates for a decline of 0.1 percent.
The surprisingly weak data powered U.S. bonds and stocks sharply higher and pushed the dollar lower.

June pesos rallied sharply on the data. Total peso volume was estimated at 13,000 contracts, exceeding total yen volume of 10,500, traders said. Volume for June pesos and June yen was estimated at about 10,000 each.

Margaret Kudarauskas, senior forex analyst at Technical Data, said cash pesos rose in a relief rally on the U.S. data. She said cash pesos sold off on Monday due to fears about strong U.S. economic growth.
"Mexican financial markets always get nervous when there is any feeling that foreign investors are disillusioned or maybe finding other rates with less risk," Kudarauskas said.
June marks rose through Monday's pit high of $0.5817, as the dollar/mark broke below 1.7250 spot.

German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt's comments added to the short-term bullish sentiment in marks, traders said. Rexrodt said he expects dollar/mark volatility if doubts about European Monetary Union continue to grow.

At the end of pit trade, June yen was up $0.000004 at $0.007937, marks were up $0.0031 at $0.5821, Swiss francs up $0.0033 at $0.6851, sterling up $0.0072 at $1.6308, Can dollars up $0.0010 at $0.7177, and pesos up $0.000900 at $0.123300.
